title: Hilary Duff ate New England clam chowder and a Dunkin’ Munchkin on stage during her Mass. concert
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Hilary Duff tried New England clam chowder and Dunkin' Munchkins during her concert in Mansfield, Massachusetts.
On her 'The Lucky Me Tour', Hilary Duff samples local fare at each stop, including regional favorites in different cities.
Duff shared her experience on stage, delighting the crowd with her reactions to the local foods she tried.

title: Adley Rutschman ready to make his debut with Red Sox on Tuesday
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman to debut with Red Sox against the Toronto Blue Jays on Tuesday after overcoming wrist inflammation.
Rutschman was acquired from the Orioles in a trade and played rehab games with Triple-A Worcester before joining the team.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy stated Rutschman won't immediately have an everyday role to manage his workload.

title: Springfield zoo suffers devastating damage during severe storm
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Springfield's The Zoo in Forest Park closed indefinitely after severe storm damage to trees and enclosures.
A state of emergency was declared in Springfield due to extensive power outages and infrastructure damage.
The zoo faces significant financial challenges from lost revenue and repair costs, with donation efforts ongoing.

title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people died in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough Monday afternoon, police report.
The crash led to the closure of the Solomon Pond Road exit on I-290 East near I-495.
Drivers are advised to use alternate routes due to expected delays and increased traffic in the area.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Shrewsbury police responded to a possible drowning at Lake Quinsigamond on Sunday afternoon near Sunset Beach.
A male victim's body was located using sonar technology early Monday in the lake after extensive search efforts.
The investigation into the drowning continues, with the victim's identity and details yet to be released.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Khalil Jacobs, undrafted from the University of Missouri, is impressing at New England Patriots training camp.
Jacobs, known for his play speed, was signed as an undrafted free agent by the Patriots in May 2026.
Jacobs is competing for a roster spot amidst a thin linebacker group, contributing significantly in practices.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed H.5595, eliminating gestational limits and expanding access to later-term abortions in Massachusetts.
The law allows abortions at or after 24 weeks based on a physician's judgment, removing restrictive criteria.
Massachusetts becomes one of 10 states without gestational limits, aiming to enhance reproductive rights amid national debates.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The gravestone of free Black man Sebastian, who died in 1729, was uncovered at Boston's Granary Burying Ground.
Believed the oldest gravestone for a free Black person in the U.S., it was restored by Boston's Historic Burying Grounds.
Sebastian, also known as Boston, previously enslaved, advocated for marriage rights, influencing early antislavery efforts.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots' Carlton Davis and Will Campbell returned to practice Monday; Campbell fully participated while Davis was limited.
Romeo Doubs made a highlight-reel catch, closing a two-minute drill; Kyle Williams also impressed with a deep catch.
Rookie tight end Tanner Arkin has transitioned from primarily playing defense in high school to offense at Colorado State.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A lifeguard was dragged underwater by a shark at Scarborough Beach State Park in Maine, officials reported.
The lifeguard freed himself and swam to shore; the beach closed for an hour following the incident.
Authorities advise caution and remind swimmers to report shark sightings and follow lifeguard instructions.
